book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook teaches each topic fully and puts questions at the end of the chapter. Here the order is the exam paper's: question first, concept second. Each statement is read, then the exact lecture node that decides it is fetched and replayed, then the verdict goes back onto the statement and is pushed through the options by elimination. Inside a question the statements are checked in the order the lecture tells them, not the paper's (Q2: the founding history decides statement III first; Q4: the borrowing figure gives the fiscal deficit before revenue and primary deficits). The Q4 primary-deficit formula is reused at once in Q5, so the learner meets the same rule twice in two minutes. Q6 finds the answer by eliminating on one false number (45% vs 41%), then confirms with one true statement. This works as retrieval practice for revision: the learner sees what an exam asks about a concept and which one node of the lesson answers it.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: One piece per exam statement: match it to the single lecture node that decides it, judge it true or false from that node, and carry the verdict to the answer options by elimination.

talmel_summary: Two layers. The narrator's own page marks (green highlighter, ticks, crosses on options, progress circles) land together with his verdict words, within about half a second, and the elimination crosses show the logic exactly as it is spoken. The meaning-carrying pictures (repay arrow, war timeline, income-group bar, deficit gap bar, devolution fork, weighted criteria bar) are inside replayed lecture clips on a filmed tablet; they play in transcript gaps and the narrator's own words come 2-10 s after as 'yahan se clear hai ki...', so relative to his voice the picture always leads. Weak: tiny tablet text, census numbers and the bovine definition never spoken, Q5 with no working drawn, and one spoken option slip (A, C, D) against the crossed a, b, d. Note: about 245 s (30%) of speech, mostly the lecture clips' audio, is missing or garbled in the transcript (15 gaps over 5 s); 10 of 24 tiles fall in such gaps.

voice.notes: About 190-200 recognised words per minute when he speaks, brisk and promotional. A fixed rhythm per question: 'chaliye ab dekhte hain question N', paraphrase of the statement, 'iske liye hum log ... folder mein jayenge', clip, 'to yahan se ye baat clear ho jati hai ki', 'statement N correct/incorrect hai', 'iska matlab option ... wrong', 'answer hua ...', and the tag 'green mark karenge'. Numbers are read in English with Hindi glue ('60,000 minus 80,000 equals to minus 20,000', 'value aayegi 48,500 crores'). Stress falls on correct/wrong and the option letter. No pauses for the learner to try a question first.

game_ideas.player_does: Gets a 'statement court' built from one chapter: 3-4 statements, each true or with exactly one changed element (a number 41% to 45%, a category non-tax to liability, an extreme word like 'single-handedly'). For each, the player drags it onto the lesson node that decides it and rules true or false.
game_ideas.process_happens: The chosen node opens as a short replay of the lesson scene (the receipts tree, the devolution fork); the changed element in a false statement lights up against the node's real value, and the options grid crosses every option that contains a false statement.
game_ideas.win: Correct verdict on each statement with the right evidence node; the surviving option is the answer.
game_ideas.lose: Ruling a false statement true shows the node with the conflicting value side by side (41% vs 45%) and leaves wrong options standing; picking the wrong node shows 'this node does not decide this statement'.
game_ideas.concept: statement elimination: one false statement removes every option that contains it

game_ideas.player_does: Elimination race (new mechanic): faces a multi-statement question with an options grid and a check budget; chooses which statement to check first, each check costs one coin.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each check reveals true or false, and the grid crosses every option the verdict rules out; a counter shows how many options each check removed.
game_ideas.win: Reach a single surviving option in the fewest checks (for Q6, checking statement II alone leaves only (c)), then make one confirming check.
game_ideas.lose: A check that removes no option is shown as 'wasted'; running out of coins with two options left forces a guess and shows which check would have split them.
game_ideas.concept: statement elimination: one false statement removes every option that contains it

game_ideas.player_does: Runs a budget: drags the question's figures (revenue receipts, revenue expenditure, capital spending, borrowing, interest, non-debt receipts) into a picture of a receipts bar, an expenditure bar and the gap.
game_ideas.process_happens: The gap block grows or shrinks; it is named fiscal deficit and must be filled by borrowing; the revenue box shows its own shortfall (revenue deficit); removing the interest slice from the gap leaves the primary deficit. Live numbers update on each block.
game_ideas.win: All figures in the right slots; the three deficits shown match a statement set or an option.
game_ideas.lose: Each wrong slot produces one of the exam's trap answers and says which mistake made it (adding interest gives 51,500; subtracting non-debt receipts again gives 58,500 in Q5).
game_ideas.concept: primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments (Q4 statement III, then Q5)

game_ideas.player_does: Sorts government money items into capital or revenue receipts and, within revenue, tax or non-tax: borrowings, disinvestment, loan recovery, interest received on loans, PSU dividends, GST.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each item flows to the government emblem; a liability meter rises only when borrowing comes in (with a return arrow for principal plus interest); an asset meter falls on disinvestment.
game_ideas.win: All items sorted, with the liability and asset meters explaining each capital receipt.
game_ideas.lose: Putting interest received under capital receipts shows the liability meter refusing to move: no one has to be repaid.
game_ideas.concept: interest received on loans is non-tax revenue, not a liability (Q1 statement III)

game_ideas.player_does: Acts as the Finance Commission: first sets the vertical share of the divisible tax pool for states, then splits the states' share across criteria weights.
game_ideas.process_happens: The pool splits centre vs states; a stacked bar of criteria fills slice by slice; sample states receive more or less as weights move (income distance favours poorer states, tax effort rewards collection).
game_ideas.win: Match the commission's recommended split and explain who gains from one criterion.
game_ideas.lose: Entering 45% shows the recommended 41% next to it; a criteria set that does not add up to 100% will not lock.
game_ideas.concept: 15th Finance Commission: 41% vertical devolution, weighted horizontal criteria incl. tax effort (Q6)

checks_learned: Spoken option letters in an elimination must match the options crossed on screen (here 'A, C and D' was said while a, b, d were crossed): a script-vs-scene check.
Every numeric question needs its working drawn on screen (formula, then numbers, then result); Q5 showed only a tick after 30 s of still page.
Every figure given in a question that the solution does not use must be named as a distractor with the reason (the 10,000 non-debt receipts in Q5).

Generated practice: each false statement must differ from a true fact in exactly one checkable element (number, category, actor or an extreme word), and must carry a link to the lesson node that refutes it.

When the answer is reached by elimination, the narration must say which statements no longer need checking and why, and one surviving statement should be confirmed positively (Q6 did the confirmation but not the explanation).
An evidence scene must restate its fact in the narration; text that only sits on screen (the bovine definition, census numbers, vertical and horizontal) does not count as taught.
BIE must not reuse lessons as filmed screens with small text; an evidence scene is re-rendered on the canvas, with the lesson's own narration line included in the script and subtitles.

Speech recognition lost about 245 s here, mostly replayed lesson audio: when BIE builds a practice video from lesson clips, the clip lines must come from the script, not from re-recognition, and any 10 s window with no recognised words is flagged.

teaching_best.why: Elimination made visible and spoken: one false statement (45% vs 41%) crosses every option that contains it, and the answer falls out without checking the other statements.
Q5 reuses the primary-deficit rule from Q4 within two minutes, so one formula is practised on two questions with different numbers.

The verdict on the Gokul Mission statement is a cause chain that follows the statement's own wording (breed improvement, rural employment, dairy economy, rural poor), so the learner sees how the exam paraphrases a lesson.
A sweeping word ('single-handedly') is refuted by one counter-example from the same lesson (IFC also works for developing countries).
The question's own numbers are put into the lesson's formula and the sign is read aloud (negative means deficit).

teaching_weak.why: First 57 s are a promotional count of questions and marks; no economics.
Every question spends 10-20 s on a filmed hand scrolling app folders; navigation, not teaching, and the lecture text on the tablet is small.
The capital-receipt definition (statement I) is lost: about 21 s of garbled recognition, so the reason statement I is true cannot be checked from the transcript.
Q5 has no working on screen and the 10,000 non-debt receipts distractor is never addressed.
Spoken slip: 'options A, C and D wrong' then 'answer C'; the screen is right (a, b, d crossed), the voice is not.
Q6 statements I and III are never checked or mentioned; the learner is not told that elimination made them unnecessary.
